lines.text: It took less than a second to make. And you couldn't tell.
In a twenty twenty-six study, people spotted AI-edited receipts fifty point one percent of the time.
A coin flip. The best forensic detectors barely beat chance.
And when the purchase is real, the reward is a point. In one of fifteen programs you joined, and forgot.
The merchant seals every receipt with a signature. Arbitrum verifies it. And your reward is real ownership, in the brand you bought from.
Here it is, live on Robinhood Chain. At the till, the merchant issues a sealed receipt. Every field, signed.
The customer scans it. Stockback checks the merchant's signature, the expiry, and whether this receipt was ever used.
One tap. One transaction. Rust on Arbitrum Stylus verifies the claim, and vault shares land in the wallet.
A real transaction, confirmed on chain.
Try to use the same receipt twice, and it's rejected. Once per receipt. For anyone.
Under the hood, Stylus verifies these signatures for up to nine times less gas than Solidity. A hundred fit in a single transaction.
Change one digit on a sealed receipt, and the seal breaks.
Shoppers own a share of what they buy. No expiry. No admin who can take it back.
Brands reward only verified purchases, on budgets they control.
